props.doc: Ticketing, chat and paging: the connectors that tell humans what happened. Low risk, high value - most of what a SOC wants automated first is this.
props.name: itsm_connectors

props.code:
def param(kind, **extra):
    """One input property, in JSON Schema terms."""
    spec = {"type": kind} if kind not in ("ipv4", "hostname") else {"type": "string"}
    spec.update(extra)
    return spec


def cmd(key, name, method, url, inputs, outputs, extract=None, risk="low",
        effect="read", doc="", techniques=None, undo=None, timeout_ms=30000,
        required=None, category="integration", body=None, success=None):
    """
    One command definition.

    Structured JSON in, structured JSON out. The output_schema is what the
    playbook validator type-checks the next step against, so a command whose
    schema lies fails at publish rather than at 03:00.
    """
    definition = {
        "key": key,
        "name": name,
        "category": category,
        "kind": "http",
        "input_schema": {
            "type": "object",
            "required": list(inputs.keys()) if required is None else required,
            "properties": inputs,
            "additionalProperties": False,
        },
        "output_schema": {"type": "object", "properties": outputs},
        "implementation": {
            "method": method,
            "url": url,
            "extract": extract or {},
            "success_codes": success or [200, 201, 202, 204],
        },
        "required_permissions": ["commands.execute"],
        "required_capabilities": ["net"],
        "timeout_ms": timeout_ms,
        "risk_level": risk,
        "effect": effect,
        "trust_level": "trusted",
        "technique_ids": techniques or [],
        "doc": doc,
    }
    if body is not None:
        definition["implementation"]["body"] = body
    if effect == "mutating":
        # A mutating command with no dry-run example would make dry run a lie,
        # and the registry validator refuses it.
        definition["dry_run_example"] = {"dry_run": True, "would_call": key}
    if undo:
        # Named, not inferred. The platform never invents a rollback.
        definition["undo_command"] = undo
    if risk == "high":
        definition["required_permissions"] = ["commands.execute", _permission_for(key)]
    return definition


def _permission_for(key):
    """High-risk commands need the response permission that matches them."""
    action = key.split(".", 1)[1]
    if "isolate" in action or "contain" in action or "quarantine_host" in action:
        return "response.isolate"
    if "block" in action:
        return "response.block"
    if "disable" in action or "suspend" in action:
        return "response.disable_account"
    if "revoke" in action or "signout" in action:
        return "response.revoke_sessions"
    if "delete" in action or "purge" in action or "remove_mail" in action:
        return "response.delete_mail"
    if "firewall" in action or "policy" in action:
        return "response.firewall"
    return "response.isolate"


def field(name, label, kind="text", required=True, default=None,
          options=None, help="", placeholder=""):
    # One thing an operator must be told before this tool can be reached.
    return {
        "name": name, "label": label, "kind": kind, "required": required,
        "default": default, "options": options or [], "help": help,
        "placeholder": placeholder,
    }


def connector(cid, name, vendor, category, auth, base_url, allowlist, commands,
              min_permissions=None, rate_limit=None, health=None,
              version="1.0.0", setup=None, derive=None, ingest=None,
              hunt=None):
    # A connector manifest. Installing one publishes its commands; no engine
    # change.
    #
    # setup is what THIS vendor needs before it can be reached, and no two
    # agree: CrowdStrike wants a cloud region, Sentinel a tenant and a
    # workspace, Splunk a host and a port. Asking every connector for a
    # client id and a secret asked the two questions they happen to share
    # and none of the ones that make a connection work.
    fields = list(setup or [])

    # Which setting the commands of this connector actually read. Most say
    # base_url; a few front a protocol that is not HTTP and say gateway_url
    # instead, and asking those for a base_url nothing reads is how a form
    # grows a field that does nothing.
    setting = "base_url"
    if "{{" in base_url:
        inner = base_url.split("{{", 1)[1].split("}}", 1)[0].strip()
        setting = inner.rsplit(".", 1)[-1] if inner else "base_url"

    if not any(f["name"] == setting for f in fields):
        # Every connector can at least be pointed elsewhere: a regional
        # cloud, a tenant-specific host, an on-premise appliance.
        # A connector whose base_url is itself a template has no host until
        # someone supplies one, so there is nothing to prefill and the field
        # is the only way the connection can exist at all.
        templated = "{{" in base_url
        fields.insert(0, field(
            setting, "API base URL", kind="url",
            default=None if templated else base_url,
            help="Change for a regional cloud or an on-premise appliance."
                 if not templated else "The hostname this tenant answers on."))

    return {
        "setup": fields,
        # Settings a vendor addresses by a composite of the ones a person
        # can actually be asked for. Nobody knows their workspace ARM id;
        # everybody knows their subscription, resource group and workspace
        # name, and the id is those three in a fixed shape.
        "derive": derive or {},
        # How this product is polled for alerts: which command lists them,
        # which turns ids into objects, and where the timestamp lives that
        # the watermark advances to. A connector without it can still
        # receive a webhook; it just cannot be asked.
        "ingest": ingest or {},
        # Which command runs an arbitrary hunt query, what the query
        # parameter is called, and what language an engineer is writing.
        # A tool without this cannot be hunted in - which is most of them,
        # because a firewall is not a place you go looking.
        "hunt": hunt or {},
        "id": cid, "name": name, "vendor": vendor, "category": category,
        "version": version, "auth": auth, "base_url": base_url,
        "egress_allowlist": allowlist,
        "min_vendor_permissions": min_permissions or [],
        "rate_limit": rate_limit or {},
        "health_check": health or {},
        "commands": commands,
        "publisher": "master-soar",
        "signature": "",
    }


servicenow = connector(
    "servicenow.itsm", "ServiceNow", "ServiceNow", "ticketing",
    {"kind": "basic", "roles": ["username", "password"]},
    "{{ integration.config.base_url }}",
    ["{{ integration.config.instance }}.service-now.com"],
    min_permissions=["sn_si.analyst", "itil"],
    health={"path": "/api/now/table/sys_user?sysparm_limit=1"},
    setup=[
        field("base_url", "Instance URL", kind="url",
              placeholder="https://client.service-now.com"),
        field("assignment_group", "Assignment group", required=False,
              help="Where tickets this SOC raises are queued."),
    ],
    commands=[
        cmd("servicenow.create_incident", "ServiceNow: Create Incident", "POST",
            "{{ integration.config.base_url }}/api/now/table/incident",
            {"short_description": param("string", maxLength=160),
             "description": param("string", maxLength=32000),
             "urgency": param("string", enum=["1", "2", "3"]),
             "impact": param("string", enum=["1", "2", "3"]),
             "assignment_group": param("string"),
             "caller_id": param("string")},
            {"sys_id": {"type": "string"}, "number": {"type": "string"}},
            {"sys_id": "$.result.sys_id", "number": "$.result.number"},
            risk="low", effect="mutating", category="ticketing",
            required=["short_description"],
            body={"short_description": "{{ inputs.short_description }}",
                  "description": "{{ inputs.description }}",
                  "urgency": "{{ inputs.urgency | default('2') }}",
                  "impact": "{{ inputs.impact | default('2') }}",
                  "assignment_group": "{{ inputs.assignment_group }}",
                  "category": "security"}),

        cmd("servicenow.update_incident", "ServiceNow: Update Incident", "PATCH",
            "{{ integration.config.base_url }}/api/now/table/incident/{{ inputs.sys_id | urlencode }}",
            {"sys_id": param("string"), "state": param("string"),
             "work_notes": param("string", maxLength=32000),
             "close_code": param("string"), "close_notes": param("string")},
            {"number": {"type": "string"}, "state": {"type": "string"}},
            {"number": "$.result.number", "state": "$.result.state"},
            risk="low", effect="mutating", category="ticketing",
            required=["sys_id"],
            body={"state": "{{ inputs.state }}",
                  "work_notes": "{{ inputs.work_notes }}",
                  "close_code": "{{ inputs.close_code }}",
                  "close_notes": "{{ inputs.close_notes }}"}),

        cmd("servicenow.get_cmdb_ci", "ServiceNow: Get CMDB Item", "GET",
            "{{ integration.config.base_url }}/api/now/table/cmdb_ci?sysparm_query=name%3D{{ inputs.name | urlencode }}",
            {"name": param("string")},
            {"items": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "object"}}},
            {"items": "$.result"},
            doc="Who owns this host, and how critical is it. The CMDB is usually "
                "the only place that knows, and the approval policy reads asset "
                "criticality from it."),
    ],
)

jira = connector(
    "atlassian.jira", "Jira", "Atlassian", "ticketing",
    {"kind": "basic", "roles": ["email", "api_token"]},
    "{{ integration.config.base_url }}",
    ["{{ integration.config.site }}.atlassian.net"],
    health={"path": "/rest/api/3/myself"},
    setup=[
        field("base_url", "Site URL", kind="url",
              placeholder="https://client.atlassian.net"),
        field("project_key", "Project key", placeholder="SEC",
              help="Where issues are created."),
        field("issue_type", "Issue type", required=False,
              default="Task"),
    ],
    commands=[
        cmd("jira.create_issue", "Jira: Create Issue", "POST",
            "{{ integration.config.base_url }}/rest/api/3/issue",
            {"project": param("string"), "summary": param("string", maxLength=255),
             "description": param("string"), "issue_type": param("string"),
             "priority": param("string"), "labels": {"type": "array",
                                                     "items": {"type": "string"}}},
            {"key": {"type": "string"}, "id": {"type": "string"}},
            {"key": "$.key", "id": "$.id"},
            risk="low", effect="mutating", category="ticketing",
            required=["project", "summary", "issue_type"],
            body={"fields": {"project": {"key": "{{ inputs.project }}"},
                             "summary": "{{ inputs.summary }}",
                             "description": "{{ inputs.description }}",
                             "issuetype": {"name": "{{ inputs.issue_type }}"},
                             "labels": "{{ inputs.labels | json }}"}}),

        cmd("jira.transition_issue", "Jira: Transition Issue", "POST",
            "{{ integration.config.base_url }}/rest/api/3/issue/{{ inputs.issue_key | urlencode }}/transitions",
            {"issue_key": param("string"), "transition_id": param("string")},
            {"transitioned": {"type": "boolean"}},
            risk="low", effect="mutating", category="ticketing", success=[204],
            body={"transition": {"id": "{{ inputs.transition_id }}"}}),

        cmd("jira.add_comment", "Jira: Add Comment", "POST",
            "{{ integration.config.base_url }}/rest/api/3/issue/{{ inputs.issue_key | urlencode }}/comment",
            {"issue_key": param("string"), "comment": param("string")},
            {"id": {"type": "string"}}, {"id": "$.id"},
            risk="low", effect="mutating", category="ticketing",
            body={"body": {"type": "doc", "version": 1,
                           "content": [{"type": "paragraph",
                                        "content": [{"type": "text",
                                                     "text": "{{ inputs.comment }}"}]}]}}),
    ],
)

slack = connector(
    "slack.v1", "Slack", "Slack", "chat",
    {"kind": "api_key", "roles": ["bot_token"], "header": "Authorization",
     "prefix": "Bearer "},
    "https://slack.com/api",
    ["slack.com"],
    min_permissions=["chat:write", "channels:read"],
    health={"path": "/auth.test"},
    setup=[
        field("default_channel", "Default channel", required=False,
              placeholder="#soc-alerts",
              help="Used when a playbook posts without naming one."),
    ],
    commands=[
        cmd("slack.post_message", "Slack: Post Message", "POST",
            "https://slack.com/api/chat.postMessage",
            {"channel": param("string"), "text": param("string", maxLength=4000),
             "blocks": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "object"}}},
            {"ts": {"type": "string"}, "ok": {"type": "boolean"}},
            {"ts": "$.ts", "ok": "$.ok"},
            risk="low", effect="mutating", category="notification",
            required=["channel", "text"],
            body={"channel": "{{ inputs.channel }}", "text": "{{ inputs.text }}"}),

        cmd("slack.post_approval", "Slack: Post Approval Request", "POST",
            "https://slack.com/api/chat.postMessage",
            {"channel": param("string"), "approval_id": param("string"),
             "summary": param("string"), "risk_level": param("string")},
            {"ts": {"type": "string"}},
            risk="low", effect="mutating", category="notification",
            doc="Posts a link to the approval, never an approve button. The decision "
                "is made in the platform where the nonce, the separation-of-duty "
                "check and the MFA step-up apply - a chat button would route around "
                "all three."),
    ],
)

teams = connector(
    "microsoft.teams", "Microsoft Teams", "Microsoft", "chat",
    {"kind": "oauth2_client", "roles": ["client_id", "client_secret"],
     "token_url": "https://login.microsoftonline.com/{{ integration.config.tenant_id }}/oauth2/v2.0/token",
     "scope": "https://graph.microsoft.com/.default"},
    "https://graph.microsoft.com",
    ["graph.microsoft.com", "login.microsoftonline.com"],
    health={"path": "/v1.0/organization"},
    setup=[
        field("tenant_id", "Entra tenant id",
              placeholder="00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000",
              help="The directory the tenant lives in. It is part of the token endpoint, so a wrong one fails at sign-in."),
        field("default_team_id", "Default team id", required=False,
              help="Used when a playbook posts without naming a team."),
    ],
    commands=[
        cmd("teams.post_message", "Teams: Post Channel Message", "POST",
            "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/teams/{{ inputs.team_id | urlencode }}/channels/{{ inputs.channel_id | urlencode }}/messages",
            {"team_id": param("string"), "channel_id": param("string"),
             "message": param("string", maxLength=28000)},
            {"id": {"type": "string"}}, {"id": "$.id"},
            risk="low", effect="mutating", category="notification",
            body={"body": {"contentType": "html", "content": "{{ inputs.message }}"}}),
    ],
)

pagerduty = connector(
    "pagerduty.v2", "PagerDuty", "PagerDuty", "paging",
    {"kind": "api_key", "roles": ["routing_key"]},
    "https://events.pagerduty.com",
    ["events.pagerduty.com", "api.pagerduty.com"],
    health={"path": "/v2/enqueue"},
    setup=[
        field("service_id", "Service id", required=False,
              help="The service a triggered incident belongs to."),
    ],
    commands=[
        cmd("pagerduty.trigger", "PagerDuty: Trigger Incident", "POST",
            "https://events.pagerduty.com/v2/enqueue",
            {"summary": param("string", maxLength=1024),
             "severity": param("string", enum=["critical", "error", "warning", "info"]),
             "dedup_key": param("string"), "source": param("string")},
            {"dedup_key": {"type": "string"}}, {"dedup_key": "$.dedup_key"},
            risk="low", effect="mutating", category="notification",
            required=["summary", "severity"], success=[202],
            body={"routing_key": "{{ credentials.routing_key }}",
                  "event_action": "trigger",
                  "dedup_key": "{{ inputs.dedup_key }}",
                  "payload": {"summary": "{{ inputs.summary }}",
                              "severity": "{{ inputs.severity }}",
                              "source": "{{ inputs.source | default('master-soar') }}"}},
            doc="dedup_key is how a playbook that fires repeatedly wakes one person "
                "once instead of forty times."),
    ],
)

return [servicenow, jira, slack, teams, pagerduty]
props.doc: Ticketing, chat and paging: the connectors that tell humans what happened. Low risk, high value - most of what a SOC wants automated first is this.
